prompt: CHALLENGE: Acid-catalyzed dehydration of 3,3-dimethyl-2-butanol (also called pinacolyl alcohol, (CH₃)₃C-CH(OH)-CH₃) gives 2,3-dimethyl-2-butene as the major alkene — NOT 3,3-dimethyl-1-butene. Why?

options.label: Loss of water gives a 2° carbocation adjacent to a quaternary carbon; a 1,2-methyl shift forms a more stable 3° carbocation; β-H loss then gives the tetrasubstituted alkene 2,3-dimethyl-2-butene.
Zaitsev's rule alone — no rearrangement needed.
Carbocation rearrangements don't happen with 3° neighbors.

explanation: The 2° cation at C2 has a 3° neighbor (C3) that can migrate a methyl group. The resulting 3° cation at C2 is lower in energy. β-H elimination gives the fully-substituted alkene. This is Markovnikov's & Zaitsev's rules on steroids — ALWAYS check for rearrangement when a 2° cation is next to a 3° or quaternary carbon.
